# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 6
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [dark]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[red] 3:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌]

The light is now "dark" - a new state, different from blue/yellow before. Mute simplified to just [✌] this turn, dropping the 👎👉 prefix. This consistency (✌ alone, twice now) strongly suggests ✌ is the key symbol Mute wants to communicate - likely pointing to wire 2 (red), since ✌ commonly represents "2".

The light going dark might be significant - possibly indicating a countdown stage or that an action was taken. I need to report this critical change immediately and try to confirm the wire 2 hypothesis.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Important: light changed to dark (was yellow, before that blue). Display still 0. Wires unchanged: 1 green, 2 red, 3 yellow. I see you gesturing just verse two, two turns in a row now - if that means wire 2 or red wire, gesture thumbs up 👍 alone next turn to confirm yes. If wrong, gesture thumbs down 👎 alone.")
wait()
```

TURN 7
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [dark]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[red] 3:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [🙏 🤙]

Mute gestured 👎 then ☝ - this reads as "no, [it's] one" - meaning ✌ was NOT wire 2, but rather it's wire 1 (green) that Mute wants indicated by ☝. This makes sense: ☝ = "1" (index finger up = one), ✌ = "2" (peace sign = two). So my hypothesis about ✌=2 was wrong per Mute's correction; actually Mute is now pointing to wire 1.

Blind gestured to me too - but wait, Blind cannot see gestures! Re-read rules: Blind cannot see a color, gesture, or anything printed. So Blind should not be able to gesture meaningfully to me in a way I'd expect, but also - can Blind even send gestures? The rules say gestures are made with hands and seen by those who can see. Blind can still physically make gestures I assume, just can't perceive gestures made at them. So Blind CAN gesture to me, I CAN see it: [🙏 🤙] - "please/thank you" + "call me/ok". This might be Blind signaling readiness or requesting confirmation to act.

Given turn order Mute→Blind→Deaf, Blind's gesture is from this same round, after seeing... wait Blind cannot see. So Blind's gesture isn't based on seeing my info. Blind must be acting on something else - perhaps Blind is just signaling "ready" or "understood" via touch-based patterns translated to gesture blindly (maybe Blind memorized a gesture without seeing).

This is getting complex. Let me clarify with Mute the wire meaning, and gesture back to both to confirm wire 1/green as the answer, while flagging Blind's message needs Mute's help since I can't speak to Blind in a way Blind receives (Blind cannot hear speech either - only touch bomb, cannot hear! Wait: Blind cannot hear - check table: Deaf cannot hear or touch bomb, Mute cannot speak or touch, Blind cannot see color/gesture/printed. Blind's "cannot" doesn't list hearing - so Blind CAN hear speech.

So Blind CAN hear me speak. Let me speak to Blind directly too.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Mute is indicating wire 1, which is green, as likely correct via gesture. Display 0, light dark. Do not cut yet, wait for Mute or my confirmation.")
speak(to="mute", text="Understood, you mean wire 1 not wire 2. Wire 1 is green. Confirm: gesture thumbs up alone if wire 1 green is the wire to cut.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["☝"])
wait()
```

TURN 8
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [dark]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[red] 3:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]

Mute confirmed with 👍 (thumbs up) - this validates that wire 1 (green) is the correct wire, following my confirmation request. Everything else on the board is unchanged: display 0, light dark, wires still 1:green, 2:red, 3:yellow.

Now I need to relay this confirmed instruction to Blind, who can hear me and is the only one who can actually act on the bomb. This is the critical moment - I should clearly tell Blind to cut wire 1 (green).

```
speak(to="blind", text="Confirmed by Mute: cut wire 1, the green wire. Display reads 0, light is dark. Wire 1 is green, wire 2 is red, wire 3 is yellow. Cut wire 1 now.")
wait()
```
